text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Young people care about the future.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Many older people think that young people are badly behaved.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
and methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify a value judgment from Hana’s statement. Explain why it is a value judgment.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Kaito is arguing that older people should hold positions of power.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Identify one fact from Kaito’s statement.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how well this fact supports Kaito’s argument.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Kaito’s or Hana’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
A government wants to improve the lives of young people.
The following actions are being considered:
• provide more education and training for young people
• lower the voting age so that young people can vote in elections
• involve young people in decision-making about local issues.
Which one of these actions would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
